author: p-wysocki
title: Debian Packages job fails — apt-get cannot connect to azure.archive.ubuntu.com

failed_jobs.name: Debian Packages / Debian Packages
failed_jobs.symptom: apt-get install fails: Unable to connect to azure.archive.ubuntu.com:80

failed_jobs.name: ci/gha_overall_status_ubuntu_24
failed_jobs.symptom: Overall status check failed because Debian Packages job failed

key_errors: E: Failed to fetch http://azure.archive.ubuntu.com/ubuntu/pool/... Unable to connect to azure.archive.ubuntu.com:80: [IP: 40.81.13.82 80]
E: Unable to fetch some archives, maybe run apt-get update or try with --fix-missing?
root_cause: The GitHub Actions runner lost connectivity to azure.archive.ubuntu.com (Ubuntu package mirror) mid-job. Multiple .deb packages across different pool paths all failed with 'Unable to connect' at the same IP (40.81.13.82:80), indicating a transient network outage on the Azure runner or the Ubuntu mirror endpoint. The PR itself (Python binding fix in async_infer_queue.cpp) is entirely unrelated to the Debian packaging job.
reproduction_steps: N/A — transient network failure on CI runner, not reproducible locally.
recommended_actions: Re-run the failed Debian Packages job to retry after the network issue clears.
If recurrent, consider adding --retry or --fix-missing fallback to apt-get install commands.
prevention_strategies: Add apt-get retry logic (e.g., apt-get install -y --fix-missing or a retry wrapper) to handle transient mirror unavailability.
historical_context: Network failures fetching from azure.archive.ubuntu.com are a known transient infrastructure issue on Azure-hosted GitHub Actions runners.
